assetCapital.asset: System Use Gas (SUG) and pipeline fuel retention
assetCapital.basis: 0.010% of transported throughput recovered by eliminating commercial fuel retention under-recovery and unaccounted-for gas (UAF) slippage (~180,000 MMBtu/yr)
assetCapital.source: ~120-130 MMSCMD (~1.8B MMBtu/yr) transported across ~16,000 km network. Under statutory access codes and open-access tariff regulations, System Use Gas (compressor station fuel, line heaters) and normative transmission loss typically total 0.8-1.2% of throughput (~14.4-21.6M MMBtu/yr). Un-reconciled compressor station fuel telemetry, meter calibration drift, and delayed regulatory fuel tracker filings routinely create commercial under-recovery of 0.05-0.15% of throughput. ₹750/MMBtu reflects the blended commodity cost of gas (~US$9/MMBtu pooled domestic and imported LNG benchmark). Recovering 0.010% of throughput value represents under one-tenth of typical commercial fuel under-recovery exposure, strictly separated from P42's capacity scheduling tariff and P38's compressor driver efficiency.

rationale: P43 Gas Contracts Analyst governs commercial natural gas transportation service agreements (TSAs/GTAs), open-access pipeline tariff compliance, secondary capacity release auctions, shipper credit exposure, monthly imbalance cash-out settlements, and statutory customer index filings across a ~16,000 km transmission network transporting 120-130 MMSCMD (~1.8B MMBtu/yr). Sizing: 25 seats represents ~0.52% of total enterprise payroll (4,800 staff), structured across contract administration & capacity release (6), nomination entitlement & path audit (5), monthly imbalance reconciliation & cash-out settlements (7), counterparty credit surveillance (4), and fuel retention & regulatory compliance (3). Asset Capital: In volume form, recovering 0.010% of transported volume (180,000 MMBtu/yr valued at ₹750/MMBtu commodity price = ₹13.5 Cr/yr) by reconciling compressor fuel burn and unaccounted-for gas (UAF) against in-kind shipper retention schedules, eliminating commercial fuel under-recovery. Asset Risk: Strictly null following the restraint of value_model.js peer commercial and scheduling roles (P15, P17, P28, P29, P42). Contracts analysts do not operate physical pipeline valves or control room pressure safeguards (owned by P14 Pipeline Controller), nor do they manage containment barrier integrity (owned by P27 Pipeline Integrity). Counterparty credit defaults and imbalance disputes represent commercial settlements rather than loss of primary containment. Resource Recovery: Strictly null as midstream transmission does not discover or produce subsurface hydrocarbons.
caveats: Never name any operator in citations or UI copy. Unified commodity rate is anchored to blended domestic and imported pooled natural gas benchmarks (~US$9.00/MMBtu or ₹750/MMBtu). Asset capital is strictly bounded to physical commodity fuel under-recovery, avoiding double-counting with P42 (transmission capacity tariffs), P14 (hydraulic control), and P38 (driver fuel burn). If an operator maintains the strictest interpretation from value_model.js that commercial analysts perform offline administration without physical critical-path gating, assetCapital can be set to null, anchoring the role's value entirely in Human Capital (~₹4.84 Cr/yr across 25 seats). If an operator alternatively seeks to parameterize catastrophic counterparty credit default as an operational risk event, a conservative parameterization would be: unitsPerYear: 250 (active shipper contracts), frequency: 0.008 (1 failure per 125 contract-years), consequence: ₹50,000,000 (uncollateralized 3-month transportation and cash-out liability), alpha: 0.30, beta: 0.40 (alpha*beta = 12.0%, expected loss avoided ₹12.0 L/yr).
